value.zh: 宣皇帝諱懿，字仲達，河內溫縣孝敬里人，姓司馬氏。
value.en: Emperor Xuan had the personal name Yi and the courtesy name Zhongda. He came from Xiaojing Ward in Wen County, Henei Commandery, and belonged to the Sima clan.
value.literal: Emperor Xuan's taboo name was Yi; his courtesy name was Zhongda. He was a native of Xiaojing Ward in Wen County in Henei, and his surname was Sima.

value.zh: 其先出自帝高陽之子重黎，為夏官祝融。
value.en: The line descended from Chongli, son of Zhuanxu, who served as Zhurong under the ancient office of Xia.
value.literal: His ancestors traced their line to Chongli, son of Emperor Gaoyang (Zhuanxu), who held the office of Zhurong under the Xia.

value.zh: 歷唐、虞、夏、商，世序其職。
value.en: Across Tang, Yu, Xia, and Shang, his forebears held that post in unbroken succession.
value.literal: Through the eras of Tang, Yu, Xia, and Shang, generation after generation they succeeded one another in that office.

value.zh: 及周，以夏官為司馬。
value.en: Under the Zhou, the old Xia office became the office of Sima, the marshal.
value.literal: Under the Zhou, the Xia ministry was styled Marshal (Sima).

value.zh: 其後程伯休父，周宣王時，以世官克平徐方，錫以官族，因而為氏。
value.en: Later, Cheng Bo Xiufu—during King Xuan of Zhou—used his hereditary charge to crush the Xu region and received a clan designation from his title; from that the Sima surname arose.
value.literal: Later Cheng Bo Xiufu, in the reign of King Xuan of Zhou, by virtue of his hereditary office conquered and pacified the Xu lands and was granted a clan name taken from his office; his descendants therefore took Sima as their surname.

value.zh: 楚漢間，司馬卬為趙將，與諸侯伐秦。
value.en: In the turmoil between Chu and Han, Sima Ang commanded troops for Zhao and marched with the alliance against Qin.
value.literal: Between Chu and Han, Sima Ang served as a Zhao general and joined the feudal lords in attacking Qin.

value.zh: 秦亡，立為殷王，都河內。
value.en: After Qin collapsed he was enthroned as king of Yin with his seat at Henei.
value.literal: When Qin fell, [Ang] was established as King of Yin and made his capital in Henei.

value.zh: 漢以其地為郡，子孫遂家焉。
value.en: The Han turned that territory into a commandery, and his line took root there.
value.literal: Han converted his territory into a commandery, and his descendants settled there.

value.zh: 自卬八世，生征西將軍鈞，字叔平。
value.en: Eight generations down from Ang came General Who Guards the West Jun, whose courtesy name was Shuping.
value.literal: Eight generations after Ang was born General Who Guards the West Jun, courtesy name Shuping.

value.zh: 鈞生豫章太守量，字公度。
value.en: Jun’s son was Liang, prefect of Yuzhang, courtesy name Gongdu.
value.literal: Jun fathered Prefect of Yuzhang Liang, courtesy name Gongdu.

value.zh: 量生潁川太守儁，字元異。
value.en: Liang’s son was Jun, prefect of Yingchuan, courtesy name Yuanyi.
value.literal: Liang fathered Prefect of Yingchuan Jun, courtesy name Yuanyi.

value.zh: 儁生京兆尹防，字建公。
value.en: Jun’s son was Fang, governor of Jingzhao, courtesy name Jiangong.
value.literal: Jun fathered Governor of the Metropolitan Region Fang, courtesy name Jiangong.

value.zh: 帝即防之第二子也。
value.en: He was the second son of Fang.
value.literal: The Emperor was Fang’s second son.

value.zh: 少有奇節，聰朗多大略，博學洽聞，伏膺儒教。
value.en: Even young he revealed unusual steadfastness—acute, far-sighted, erudite, and steeped in the Confucian canon.
value.literal: In youth he showed uncommon integrity; he was bright and broad in strategic grasp, widely read and well informed, and devoted himself to Confucian teaching.

value.zh: 漢末大亂，常慨然有憂天下心。
value.en: As Han unraveled, he was repeatedly consumed by anxiety for the empire.
value.literal: At the end of Han, when great turmoil arose, he often felt stirred with concern for the realm.

value.zh: 南陽太守同郡楊俊名知人，[1]見帝，未弱冠，以為非常之器。
value.en: Yang Jun of Nanyang—his fellow townsman and a celebrated judge of talent—met him before his cap-and-girdle ceremony and pronounced him a figure of rare promise.
value.literal: Yang Jun of the same commandery, prefect of Nanyang, famed for judging men,[1] met the Emperor before his twentieth year and deemed him an extraordinary vessel.

value.zh: 尚書清河崔琰與帝兄朗善，亦謂朗曰：「君弟聰亮明允，剛斷英特，非子所及也。」
value.en: Cui Yan of Qinghe, who served in the Secretariat, was close to his elder brother Sima Lang and told Lang, “Your brother combines lucidity with integrity and carries an iron decisiveness—you cannot rival him.”
value.literal: Minister Cui Yan of Qinghe was on good terms with the Emperor’s elder brother Lang and also said to Lang, “Your younger brother is clear-sighted and fair-minded, resolute and extraordinary—not someone you can match.”

value.zh: 九年春三月，黃門張當私出掖庭才人石英等十一人，與曹爽為伎人。
value.en: Yellow Gate Zhang Dang secretly brought eleven palace talents including Shi Ying out of the inner court as entertainers for Cao Shuang.
value.literal: Spring third month ninth year—Yellow Gate Zhang Dang secretly brought eleven palace talents including Shi Ying out of the forbidden precincts as entertainers for Cao Shuang.

value.zh: 爽、晏謂帝疾篤，遂有無君之心，與當密謀，圖危社稷，期有日矣。
value.en: They thought Sima Yi dying and schemed usurpation with Zhang Dang.
value.literal: Shuang and Yan deemed the Emperor mortally ill—thereupon harbored disloyal intent—plotting secretly with Dang to endanger the altars—a date was set.

value.zh: 帝亦潛為之備，爽之徒屬亦頗疑帝。
value.en: Sima Yi armed in shadows while Shuang’s men sniffed trap.
value.literal: The Emperor also secretly prepared; Shuang’s followers likewise suspected the Emperor.

value.zh: 會河南尹李勝將莅荊州，來候帝。
value.en: When the Governor of Henan, Li Sheng, was about to take up Jingzhou, he came to visit the emperor.
value.literal: When Governor of Henan Li Sheng was about to take up Jingzhou he came to visit the Emperor.

value.zh: 帝詐疾篤，使兩婢侍，持衣衣落，指口言渴，婢進粥，帝不持杯飲，粥皆流出霑胸。
value.en: He staged palsy—maids, spilled porridge, sodden robes.
value.literal: The Emperor feigned grave illness—had two maids attend—when dressing let clothes fall—pointed to mouth saying thirst—maids brought gruel—the Emperor could not hold cup—gruel spilled soaking chest.

value.zh: 勝曰：「眾情謂明公舊風發動，何意尊體乃爾！」
value.en: Sheng said, "Everyone thought Your Lordship's old wind illness had acted up. How could your honored body be like this!"
value.literal: Sheng said, "Everyone thought Your Lordship's old wind illness had acted up. How could your honored body be like this!"

value.zh: 帝使聲氣纔屬，說「年老枕疾，死在旦夕。
value.en: The emperor made his voice and breath barely connect and said, "I am old and bedridden with illness; death is at morning or evening.
value.literal: The emperor made his voice and breath barely connect and said, "I am old and bedridden with illness; death is at morning or evening.

value.zh: 君當屈并州，并州近胡，善為之備。
value.en: You are going to serve in Bingzhou. Bingzhou is close to the Hu; prepare well for it.
value.literal: You are going to serve in Bingzhou. Bingzhou is close to the Hu; prepare well for it.

value.zh: 恐不復相見，以子師、昭兄弟為託」。
value.en: I fear we will not see each other again, so I entrust my sons Shi and Zhao, the brothers, to you."
value.literal: I fear we will not see each other again, so I entrust my sons Shi and Zhao, the brothers, to you."

value.zh: 勝曰：「當還忝本州，非并州。」
value.en: Sheng said, "I am returning to serve in my home province, not Bingzhou."
value.literal: Sheng said, "I am returning to serve in my home province, not Bingzhou."

value.zh: 帝乃錯亂其辭曰：「君方到并州。」
value.en: The emperor then deliberately confused his words and said, "You are just going to Bingzhou."
value.literal: The emperor then deliberately confused his words and said, "You are just going to Bingzhou."

value.zh: 勝復曰：「當忝荊州。」
value.en: Sheng again said, "I am going to serve in Jingzhou."
value.literal: Sheng again said, "I am going to serve in Jingzhou."

value.zh: 帝曰：「年老意荒，不解君言。
value.en: The emperor said, "In old age my mind is confused, and I did not understand your words.
value.literal: The emperor said, "In old age my mind is confused, and I did not understand your words.

value.zh: 今還為本州，盛德壯烈，好建功勳！」
value.en: Now you are returning to your home province; with flourishing virtue and vigorous valor, build fine achievements!"
value.literal: Now you are returning to your home province; with flourishing virtue and vigorous valor, build fine achievements!"

value.zh: 勝退告爽曰：「司馬公尸居餘氣，形神已離，不足慮矣。」
value.en: After Sheng withdrew, he told Shuang, "Sima Gong lies like a corpse with only remnant breath; his form and spirit have already separated. He is not worth worrying about."
value.literal: After Sheng withdrew, he told Shuang, "Sima Gong lies like a corpse with only remnant breath; his form and spirit have already separated. He is not worth worrying about."

value.zh: 他日，又言曰：「太傅不可復濟，令人愴然。」
value.en: Another day, he also said, "The Grand Tutor can no longer be saved; it makes one grieve."
value.literal: Another day, he also said, "The Grand Tutor can no longer be saved; it makes one grieve."

value.zh: 故爽等不復設備。
value.en: Shuang stood down his guard.
value.literal: Therefore Shuang and others ceased preparing defenses.

value.zh: 二年春正月，天子命帝立廟于洛陽，置左右長史，增掾屬、舍人滿十人，歲舉掾屬任御史、秀才各一人，增官騎百人，鼓吹十四人，封子肜平樂亭侯，倫安樂亭侯。
value.en: Spring year two: Luoyang ancestral shrine, full clerical staff, ten advisors, yearly recommendations, hundred escorts, fourteen pipes—sons Rong and Lun petty marquises.
value.literal: Second year spring first month—the Son of Heaven ordered the Emperor to erect a temple in Luoyang, assign left and right senior clerks, enlarge aides and attendants to ten men fully, annually nominate one aide each for censor and xiucai, add one hundred official riders and fourteen musicians, enfeoff son Rong as marquis of Pingle ting and Lun as marquis of Anle ting.

value.zh: 帝以久疾不任朝請，每有大事，天子親幸第以諮訪焉。
value.en: Too ill for court—emperor rode to his gate for counsel.
value.literal: The Emperor because of long illness could not attend court audiences—whenever great affairs arose the Son of Heaven personally visited his mansion for consultation.

value.zh: 孝惠皇帝諱衷，字正度，武帝第二子也。
value.en: Emperor Hui, whose personal name was Sima Zhong and courtesy name Zhengdu, was Emperor Wu’s second son.
value.literal: The Filial and Kind Emperor, taboo name Zhong, courtesy name Zhengdu, was the second son of Emperor Wu.

value.zh: 泰始三年，立爲皇太子，時年九歲。
value.en: In 267, when he was nine years old, he was named heir apparent.
value.literal: In the third year of Taishi, he was established as crown prince; at the time he was nine sui.

value.zh: 太熙元年四月己酉，武帝崩。
value.en: In the fourth month of the first year of Taixi, on the day jiyou, Emperor Wu died.
value.literal: In the first year of Taixi, on the jiyou day of the fourth month, Emperor Wu died.

value.zh: 是日，皇太子即皇帝位，大赦，改元爲永熙。
value.en: That same day the heir apparent ascended the throne, ordered a general amnesty, and adopted the reign title Yongxi.
value.literal: That same day the crown prince assumed the imperial throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Yongxi.

value.zh: 尊皇后楊氏曰皇太后，立妃賈氏爲皇后。
value.en: Empress Yang was elevated to empress dowager, and his consort Lady Jia was installed as empress.
value.literal: The empress, Lady Yang, was honored as empress dowager; Consort Jia was established as empress.

value.zh: 八月庚申，以趙王倫爲征東將軍、都督徐兗二州諸軍事；
value.en: Prince Lun of Zhao was named general who conquers the east and given joint command over Xu and Yan;
value.literal: In the eighth month, on the gengshen day, Prince Lun of Zhao was made general who conquers the east and area commander for military affairs in Xu and Yan provinces;

value.zh: 河間王顒爲北中郎將，鎮鄴；
value.en: Prince Yong of Hejian became a northern camp general and garrisoned Ye;
value.literal: Prince Yong of Hejian was made general of the northern gentlemen of the household and stationed at Ye;

value.zh: 太子太師何劭爲都督豫州諸軍事，鎮許昌。
value.en: He Shao, the heir apparent’s grand preceptor, took command in Yu Province from a base at Xuchang.
value.literal: Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent He Shao was made area commander for military affairs in Yu Province and stationed at Xuchang.

value.zh: 徙長沙王乂爲常山王。
value.en: Prince Yi of Changsha was re-enfeoffed as prince of Changshan.
value.literal: Prince Yi of Changsha was transferred to be prince of Changshan.

value.zh: 己巳，進西陽公羕爵爲王。
value.en: Duke Yang of Xiyang was raised to princely rank.
value.literal: On the jisi day, Duke Yang of Xiyang was advanced in noble rank to prince.

value.zh: 辛未，立隴西世子越爲東海王。
value.en: Yue, heir of the house of Longxi, was created prince of Donghai.
value.literal: On the xinwei day, heir apparent Yue of Longxi was established as prince of Donghai.

value.zh: 五月，荊、揚二州大水。
value.en: Jing and Yang provinces were overwhelmed by flood in the fifth month.
value.literal: In the fifth month, Jing and Yang provinces suffered great flooding.

value.zh: 匈奴郝散弟度元帥馮翊、北地馬蘭羌、盧水胡反，攻北地，太守張損死之。
value.en: Du Yuan, Hao San’s brother, led Qiang and Lushui Hu allies from Fengyi and Beidi in revolt, stormed Beidi, and killed Prefect Zhang Sun in the fighting.
value.literal: Hao San’s younger brother of the Xiongnu, Du Yuan, led the Fengyi, Beidi Malan Qiang, and Lushui Hu in rebellion, attacked Beidi, and Prefect Zhang Sun died in it.

value.zh: 馮翊太守歐陽建與度元戰，建敗績。
value.en: Ouyang Jian, prefect of Fengyi, met Du Yuan in battle and suffered a rout.
value.literal: Fengyi Prefect Ouyang Jian battled with Du Yuan; Jian was defeated.

value.zh: 徵征西大將軍、趙王倫爲車騎將軍，以太子太保、梁王肜爲征西大將軍、都督雍梁二州諸軍事，鎮關中。
value.en: Prince Lun of Zhao was recalled from the western command to the capital post of general of chariots and cavalry, while Prince Rong of Liang took his place as general-in-chief in the west with authority over Yong and Liang and a mandate to hold the Guanzhong frontier.
value.literal: General-in-chief who conquers the west, Prince Lun of Zhao, was summoned to be general of chariots and cavalry; Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Prince Rong of Liang, was made general-in-chief who conquers the west and area commander for military affairs in Yong and Liang provinces, garrisoning within the passes.

value.zh: 永康元年春正月癸亥朔，大赦，改元。
value.en: The new moon of the first month of Yongkang brought a general amnesty and a new reign title.
value.literal: In the first year of Yongkang, spring, first month, on the guihai new moon, a general amnesty; the era name was changed.

value.zh: 己卯，日有蝕之。
value.en: The sun was eclipsed on the jimao day.
value.literal: On the jimao day, there was a solar eclipse.

value.zh: 丙子，皇孫𧇃卒。
value.en: On the bingzi day the imperial grandson died.
value.literal: On the bingzi day, the imperial grandson 𧇃 died.

value.zh: 夏四月辛卯，日有蝕之。
value.en: Another solar eclipse occurred on the xinmao day in the fourth month.
value.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the xinmao day, there was a solar eclipse.

value.zh: 癸巳，梁王肜、趙王倫矯詔廢賈后爲庶人，司空張華、尚書僕射裴頠皆遇害，侍中賈謐及黨與數十人皆伏誅。
value.en: On the guisi day Princes Xiong and Lun forged an edict that deposed Empress Jia; Zhang Hua and Pei Wei were killed, and Jia Mi with dozens of his partisans went to the execution ground.
value.literal: On the guisi day, Prince Xiong of Liang and Prince Lun of Zhao forged an edict deposing Empress Jia to commoner status; Minister of Works Zhang Hua and Vice Director of the Secretariat Pei Wei both met harm and died; Palace Attendant Jia Mi and several tens of his faction were all executed.

value.zh: 甲午，倫矯詔大赦，自爲相國、都督中外諸軍，如宣文輔魏故事，追復故皇太子位。
value.en: The next day Prince Lun forged a general amnesty, named himself chancellor and commander-in-chief on the model of Sima Yi and Sima Zhao, and posthumously reinstated the murdered crown prince.
value.literal: On the jiawu day, Lun forged an edict for a general amnesty, made himself chancellor of state and area commander for all military affairs within and without, according to the old precedent of Xuan and Wen assisting Wei, and posthumously restored the former crown prince’s position.

value.zh: 丁酉，以梁王肜爲太宰，左光祿大夫何劭爲司徒，右光祿大夫劉寔爲司空，淮南王允爲驃騎將軍。
value.en: Prince Xiong became grand steward, He Shao minister of education, Liu Shi minister of works, and Prince Yun of Huainan general of agile cavalry on the dingyou day.
value.literal: On the dingyou day, Prince Xiong of Liang was made grand steward; Left Household Grandee He Shao was made minister of education; Right Household Grandee Liu Shi was made minister of works; Prince Yun of Huainan was made general of agile cavalry.

value.zh: 己亥，趙王倫矯詔害賈庶人于金墉城。
value.en: On the jihai day Prince Lun had the deposed Empress Jia killed inside the Jinyong fortress.
value.literal: On the jihai day, Prince Lun of Zhao forged an edict and harmed the commoner Jia at the Jinyong Fortress.

value.zh: 永寧元年春正月乙丑，趙王倫篡帝位。
value.en: On the yichou day in the first month of Yongning, Prince Lun of Zhao seized the throne.
value.literal: In the first year of Yongning, spring, first month, on the yichou day, Prince Lun of Zhao usurped the imperial throne.

value.zh: 丙寅，遷帝于金墉城，號曰太上皇，改金墉曰永昌宮。
value.en: The next day the true emperor was bundled off to the Jinyong fortress as a nominal “supreme emperor,” and the compound was renamed Yongchang Palace.
value.literal: On the bingyin day, the emperor was moved to the Jinyong Fortress, titled supreme emperor; Jinyong was changed to Yongchang Palace.

value.zh: 廢皇太孫臧爲濮陽王。
value.en: The heir’s son Sima Zang was demoted to prince of Puyang.
value.literal: The imperial grandson-heir Zang was deposed to be prince of Puyang.

value.zh: 五星經天，縱橫無常。
value.en: All five naked-eye planets were seen wheeling across the daytime sky in disorderly paths.
value.literal: The five planets crossed the sky, vertically and horizontally without constancy.

value.zh: 癸酉，倫害濮陽王臧。
value.en: Prince Lun had Sima Zang, now prince of Puyang, murdered on the guiyou day.
value.literal: On the guiyou day, Lun killed Prince Zang of Puyang.

value.zh: 略陽流人李特殺趙廞，傳首京師。
value.en: The refugee leader Li Te slew Zhao Xin and forwarded his head to Luoyang.
value.literal: Lüeyang migrant Li Te killed Zhao Xin and sent his head to the capital.

value.zh: 三月，平東將軍、齊王冏起兵以討倫，傳檄州郡，屯于陽翟。
value.en: In the third month Prince Jiong of Qi, general who pacifies the east, mobilized against Prince Lun, circulated a call to arms through every province, and camped at Yangzhai.
value.literal: In the third month, General Who Pacifies the East, Prince Jiong of Qi, raised troops to attack Lun, transmitted proclamations to the provinces and commanderies, and encamped at Yangzhai.

value.zh: 征北大將軍、成都王穎，征西大將軍、河間王顒，常山王乂，豫州刺史李毅，兗州刺史王彥，南中郎將、新野公歆，皆舉兵應之，眾數十萬。
value.en: Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu and Grand General Who Campaigns North; Sima Yong, Prince of Hejian and Grand General Who Campaigns West; Sima Yi, Prince of Changshan; Li Yi, inspector of Yu Province; Wang Yan, inspector of Yan Province; and Xin, Duke of Xinye and General of the Southern Gentlemen-of-the-Household, all raised armies in response, mustering several hundred thousand men.
value.literal: General-in-chief who conquers the north, Prince Ying of Chengdu; general-in-chief who conquers the west, Prince Yong of Hejian; Prince Yi of Changshan; Inspector of Yu Province Li Yi; Inspector of Yan Province Wang Yan; General of the Southern Gentlemen of the Household, Duke Xin of Xinye—all raised troops in response; the hosts numbered several hundred thousand.

value.zh: 倫遣其將閭和出伊闕，張泓、孫輔出堮阪以距冏，孫會、士猗、許超出黃橋以距穎。
value.en: Prince Lun sent Lü He through the Yique pass, Zhang Hong and Sun Fu over the E ridge to block Prince Jiong, and Sun Hui, Shi Yi, and Xu Chao from Huang Bridge to stop Prince Ying.
value.literal: Lun dispatched his generals Lü He out of Yique, Zhang Hong and Sun Fu out of E Slope to resist Jiong, and Sun Hui, Shi Yi, and Xu Chao out of Huang Bridge to resist Ying.

value.zh: 及穎將趙驤、石超戰于湨水，會等大敗，棄軍走。
value.en: At the Ju River, Zhao Xiang and Shi Chao, serving Prince Ying, routed Sun Hui’s army, which broke and ran.
value.literal: When Ying’s generals Zhao Xiang and Shi Chao battled at the Ju River, Hui and the others were greatly defeated and abandoned the army and fled.

value.zh: 夏四月，歲星晝見。
value.en: Jupiter shone visible in broad daylight during the fourth month.
value.literal: In summer, the fourth month, the year star was seen in daytime.

value.zh: 冏將何勖、盧播擊張泓於陽翟，大破之，斬孫輔等。
value.en: He Xu and Lu Bo, under Prince Jiong, crushed Zhang Hong at Yangzhai and executed Sun Fu among others.
value.literal: Jiong’s generals He Xu and Lu Bo attacked Zhang Hong at Yangzhai, greatly defeated him, and beheaded Sun Fu and others.

value.zh: 辛酉，左衛將軍王輿與尚書、淮陵王漼勒兵入宮，禽倫黨孫秀、孫會、許超、士猗、駱休等，皆斬之。
value.en: On the xinyou day Wang Yu and Prince Cui of Huailing forced the palace gates, seized Lun’s confederates Sun Xiu, Sun Hui, Xu Chao, Shi Yi, Luo Xiu, and others, and put them all to the sword.
value.literal: On the xinyou day, General of the Left Guards Wang Yu, together with the minister, Prince Cui of Huailing, led troops into the palace, captured Lun’s faction Sun Xiu, Sun Hui, Xu Chao, Shi Yi, Luo Xiu, and others; all were beheaded.

value.zh: 逐倫歸第，即日乘輿反正。
value.en: Prince Lun was sent home under guard, and the emperor was restored to the throne that same day.
value.literal: They expelled Lun to return to his residence; that same day the imperial carriage returned to rectitude.

value.zh: 群臣頓首謝罪，帝曰：「非諸卿之過也。」
value.en: The ministers prostrated themselves in apology, but the emperor told them, “None of this was your doing.”
value.literal: The host of ministers knocked their heads in admitting guilt; the emperor said, “It is not the fault of you various ministers.”

value.zh: 癸亥，詔曰：「朕以不德，纂承皇統，遠不能光濟大業，靖綏四方；
value.en: On the guihai day an edict began: “Lacking virtue, I yet inherited the throne, and I have not been able to extend the great enterprise or bring peace to the four quarters of the realm;
value.literal: On the guihai day, an edict stated: “I, lacking virtue, have succeeded to the imperial line; afar I have been unable to brighten and aid the great enterprise and pacify and soothe the four directions;

value.zh: 近不能開明刑威，式遏姦宄，至使逆臣孫秀敢肆凶虐，窺間王室，遂奉趙王倫饕據天位。
value.en: Near at hand I failed to make law and majesty clear enough to stop treason, so the rebel Sun Xiu could brutalize the court, tear at the royal house, and help Prince Lun of Zhao seize the throne by force.
value.literal: Near I have been unable to open and clarify punishments and might and check villainy and treachery, so that the rebellious minister Sun Xiu dared unleash cruelty and violence, spy on and divide the royal house, and thereupon supporting Prince Lun of Zhao greedily seized the heavenly position.

value.zh: 鎮東大將軍、齊王冏，征北大將軍、成都王穎，征西大將軍、河間王顒，並以明德茂親，忠規允著，首建大策，匡救國難。
value.en: General-in-chief who guards the east Prince Jiong of Qi, general-in-chief who conquers the north Prince Ying of Chengdu, and general-in-chief who conquers the west Prince Yong of Hejian are men of shining virtue and eminent kinship whose loyal counsel stood the test; they first devised the great plan that delivered the state from disaster.
value.literal: General-in-chief who guards the east, Prince Jiong of Qi; general-in-chief who conquers the north, Prince Ying of Chengdu; general-in-chief who conquers the west, Prince Yong of Hejian—all with bright virtue as flourishing kin, loyal plans truly manifest, first established the great strategy and rectified and saved the state’s crisis.

value.zh: 尚書漼共立大謀，左衛將軍王輿與群公卿士，協同謀略，親勒本營，斬秀及其二子。
value.en: Minister Cui framed the decisive plot; Wang Yu, general of the left guards, with the high ministers acting in concert, led their household troops into the palace and slew Sun Xiu together with his two sons.
value.literal: Minister Cui together established the great plan; General of the Left Guards Wang Yu, together with the host of dukes, ministers, and gentlemen, coordinated in stratagem, personally commanded the original camp, and beheaded Xiu and his two sons.

value.zh: 前趙王倫爲秀所誤，與其子等已詣金墉迎朕幽宮，旋軫閶闔。
value.en: The former Prince Lun of Zhao was deceived by Sun Xiu; he and his sons had already reached the Jinyong compound to bring me out of confinement and were turning their carriages toward the Changhe Gate.
value.literal: The former Prince Lun of Zhao was misled by Xiu; together with his sons and others he had already gone to Jinyong to welcome me from the hidden palace, turning the carriage at Changhe.

value.zh: 豈在予一人獨饗其慶，宗廟社稷實有賴焉。」
value.en: How could the blessing rest on me alone? The ancestral shrines and the altars of soil and grain have truly depended on them.”
value.literal: How could it be that I alone partake of the blessing? The ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain truly have relied on this.”

value.zh: 於是大赦，改元，孤寡賜穀五斛，大酺五日。
value.en: With the edict closed, the court ordered a general amnesty, a new reign title, five hu of grain for every widow, widower, and orphan, and five days of public feasting.
value.literal: Thereupon a general amnesty; the era name was changed; widowers, widows, and orphans were granted grain, five hu; great feasting for five days.

value.zh: 誅趙王倫、義陽王威、九門侯質等及倫之黨與。
value.en: Prince Lun, Prince Wei of Yiyang, Marquis Zhi of the Nine Gates, and the rest of Lun’s clique were put to death.
value.literal: Prince Lun of Zhao, Prince Wei of Yiyang, Marquis Zhi of Jiumen, and others, and Lun’s factional followers, were executed.

value.zh: 九月甲午，大將軍、秦王柬薨。
value.en: On jiawu in the ninth month, Sima Jian, Prince of Qin and Great General, died.
value.literal: In the ninth month, on jiawu, Jian, Prince of Qin and Great General, died.

value.zh: 辛丑，徵征西大將軍、梁王肜爲衛將軍、錄尚書事，以趙王倫爲征西大將軍、都督雍梁二州諸軍事。
value.en: On xinchou, Sima Rong, Prince of Liang and Great General Who Conquers the West, was recalled as General of the Guards and manager of Secretariat affairs. Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao, became Great General Who Conquers the West and commander of military affairs in Yong and Liang provinces.
value.literal: On xinchou, Rong, Prince of Liang and Great General Who Conquers the West, was summoned to be General of the Guards and manager of Secretariat affairs; Lun, Prince of Zhao, was made Great General Who Conquers the West and commander-in-chief of military affairs in Yong and Liang provinces.

value.zh: 秋八月，淮南王允舉兵討趙王倫，不克，允及其二子秦王郁、漢王迪皆遇害。
value.en: In the eighth month of autumn, Sima Yun, Prince of Huainan, raised troops against Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao, but failed. Yun and his sons Yu, Prince of Qin, and Di, Prince of Han, were all killed.
value.literal: In autumn, in the eighth month, Yun, Prince of Huainan, raised troops to attack Lun, Prince of Zhao, but could not succeed; Yun and his two sons, Yu, Prince of Qin, and Di, Prince of Han, were all killed.

value.zh: 曲赦洛陽。
value.en: A special pardon was granted in Luoyang.
value.literal: A special pardon was issued for Luoyang.

value.zh: 平東將軍、彭城王植薨。
value.en: Sima Zhi, Prince of Pengcheng and General Who Pacifies the East, died.
value.literal: Zhi, Prince of Pengcheng and General Who Pacifies the East, died.

value.zh: 改封吳王晏爲賓徒縣王。
value.en: Sima Yan, Prince of Wu, was redesignated Prince of Bintu county.
value.literal: Yan, Prince of Wu, was reassigned as Prince of Bintu county.

value.zh: 以齊王冏爲平東將軍，鎮許昌；
value.en: Sima Jiong, Prince of Qi, was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and stationed at Xuchang;
value.literal: Jiong, Prince of Qi, was made General Who Pacifies the East and stationed at Xuchang;

value.zh: 光祿大夫陳準爲太尉、錄尚書事。
value.en: Chen Zhun, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, became Grand Commandant and manager of Secretariat affairs.
value.literal: Chen Zhun, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, was made Grand Commandant and manager of Secretariat affairs.

value.zh: 月五星犯列舍經星變附見
value.en: The Moon and the Five Planets Transgressing the Lodges and Classical Stars, with Supplementary Notes on Celestial Portents.
value.literal: Transgressions of the Moon and the Five Planets against the Lodges and Classical Stars; appended observations on anomalies.

value.zh: 惠帝元康三年四月，熒惑守太微六十日。
value.en: Emperor Hui’s Yuan-kang 3 fourth month held Mars sixty days inside the Supreme Palace.
value.literal: In the fourth month of Yuan-kang 3 of Emperor Hui Spark-Delight stationed in the Supreme Palace for sixty days.

value.zh: 占曰：「諸侯三公謀其上，必有斬臣。」
value.en: The prognostication said, "Feudal lords and the Three Dukes plot against their superior; there will certainly be ministers who are beheaded."
value.literal: The omen-text says: “Marquises and the Three Dukes plot against their ruler; there must be executed ministers.

value.zh: 一曰：「天子亡國。」
value.en: One reading said, "The Son of Heaven loses the state."
value.literal: Another saying: “The Son of Heaven loses his state.

value.zh: 是春太白守畢，至是百餘日。
value.en: The same spring Venus lodged in the Net for over a hundred days.
value.literal: That spring the Great White stationed at the Net, and by then it had remained more than a hundred days.

value.zh: 占曰：「有急令之憂。」
value.en: The prognostication said, "There will be anxiety from urgent ordinances."
value.literal: The omen-text says: “There will be fear of sudden edicts.

value.zh: 一曰：「相死。」
value.en: One reading said, "The chancellor will die."
value.literal: Another saying: “The minister will die.

value.zh: 又為邊境不安。
value.en: It further signals disturbed borders.
value.literal: It also means uneasy frontiers.

value.zh: 後賈后陷殺太子。
value.en: Empress Jia later destroyed the crown prince by false accusation.
value.literal: Afterward Empress Jia framed and murdered the heir apparent.

value.zh: 六年十月乙未，太白晝見。
value.en: On yiwei in the sixth year’s tenth month Venus appeared by daylight.
value.literal: On yiwei in the tenth month of the sixth year the Great White was seen in daytime.

value.zh: 九年六月，熒惑守心。
value.en: The ninth year’s sixth month again placed Mars on the Heart.
value.literal: In the sixth month of the ninth year Spark-Delight stationed at the Heart.

value.zh: 占曰：「王者惡之。」
value.en: The prognostication said, "The king hates it."
value.literal: The omen-text says: “The king finds it ill-omened.

value.zh: 八月，熒惑入羽林。
value.en: That August Mars entered the imperial guard stars.
value.literal: In the eighth month Spark-Delight entered the Forbidden Guards asterism.

value.zh: 占曰：「禁兵大起。」
value.en: The prognostication said, "The palace troops will greatly rise."
value.literal: The omen-text says: “Palace troops will rise in force.

value.zh: 其後，帝見廢為太上皇，俄而三王起兵討趙王倫，倫悉遣中軍兵相距累月。
value.en: The emperor was soon reduced to Retired Emperor; then the three princes rose against Sima Lun, who threw the central corps against them for months.
value.literal: Thereafter the emperor was deposed as Retired Emperor; presently the Three Princes raised troops against Prince Zhao Lun, who dispatched the central army to oppose them for months on end.

value.zh: 永康元年三月，中台星坼，太白晝見。
value.en: Yongkang 1’s third month saw the asterism of the high ministers fracture while Venus shone in daylight.
value.literal: In the third month of Yongkang 1 the central terrace stars split, and the Great White appeared by day.

value.zh: 占曰：「台星失常，三公憂。
value.en: The prognostication said, "When the Terrace Stars lose their norm, the Three Dukes will have anxiety.
value.literal: The omen-text says: “When terrace stars lose their norm, the Three Dukes grieve.

value.zh: 太白晝見，為不臣。」
value.en: When Venus appears by day, it means disloyal ministers."
value.literal: The Great White seen by daylight means disloyal subjects.

value.zh: 是月，賈后殺太子，趙王倫尋廢殺後，斬司空張華。
value.en: That month Empress Jia slew the heir; Sima Lun rapidly ousted and killed her and executed Zhang Hua.
value.literal: That month Empress Jia killed the heir apparent; Prince Zhao Lun soon deposed and murdered the empress and beheaded Minister of Works Zhang Hua.

value.zh: 其五月，熒惑入南斗。
value.en: The fifth month brought Mars into the Southern Dipper.
value.literal: That fifth month Spark-Delight entered the Southern Dipper.

value.zh: 占曰：「宰相死，兵大起。
value.en: The prognostication said, "The chancellor will die, and war will greatly arise.
value.literal: The omen-text says: “The chief minister will die; troops rise on a grand scale.

value.zh: 斗，又吳分野。」
value.en: Dipper is also Wu’s allotment."
value.literal: The Dipper also marks Wu’s celestial field.

value.zh: 是時，趙王倫為相，明年，篡位，三王興師誅之。
value.en: Sima Lun held the premiership, seized the throne the following year, then fell to princely coalitions.
value.literal: At that time Prince Zhao Lun was chancellor; the next year he usurped the throne, and princes raised armies and executed him.

value.zh: 太安二年，石冰破揚州。
value.en: Tai’an 2 saw Shi Bing overrun Yangzhou.
value.literal: In the second year of Tai’an Shi Bing captured Yangzhou.

value.zh: 其八月，熒惑入箕。
value.en: That August Mars entered the Winnowing Basket.
value.literal: That eighth month Spark-Delight entered the Winnowing Basket.

value.zh: 占曰：「人主失位，兵起。」
value.en: The prognostication said, "The ruler of men loses his position, and war arises."
value.literal: The omen-text says: “The ruler loses his throne; troops arise.

value.zh: 明年趙王倫篡位，改元。
value.en: The following year Sima Lun seized the throne and altered the reign title.
value.literal: The next year Prince Zhao Lun usurped the throne and changed the era name.

value.zh: 二年二月，太白出西方，逆行入東井。
value.en: The second year’s second month brought Venus out in the west, retrograding into the Eastern Well.
value.literal: In the second month of the second year the Great White emerged in the west and moved retrograde into the Eastern Well.

value.zh: 占曰：「國失政，大臣為亂。」
value.en: The prognostication said, "The state loses its government, and great ministers make disorder."
value.literal: The omen-text says: “The state loses good government; great ministers make rebellion.

value.zh: 是時，齊王冏起兵討趙王倫，倫滅，冏擁兵不朝，專權淫奢，明年，誅死。
value.en: Prince Qi’s coalition destroyed Lun, yet Jiong quartered troops outside the capital, ruled tyrannically, and was killed the next year.
value.literal: At that time Prince Qi Jiong raised troops against Prince Zhao Lun; Lun was destroyed, but Jiong kept his army from court, monopolized power, and indulged in arrogance and luxury; the next year he was executed.

value.zh: 惠帝元康五年四月，有星孛於奎，至軒轅、太微，經三台、太陵。
value.en: Yuan-kang 5 comet crossed capital stars.
value.literal: In Yuan-kang 5 fourth month a broom star appeared in Striding Legs reaching Chariot and Supreme Palace crossing Three Steps and Great Mound.

value.zh: 占曰：「奎為魯，又為庫兵，軒轅為後宮，太微天子庭，三台為三司，太陵有積尸死喪之事。」
value.en: The prognostication said, "Legs is Lu and also arsenal troops; Xuanyuan is the rear palace; the Supreme Palace is the Son of Heaven’s court; the Three Terraces are the Three Offices; Great Mound has affairs of piled corpses, death, and mourning."
value.literal: The omen-text says: “Striding Legs is Lu and armory stores; Chariot Shaft is harem; Supreme Palace the court; Three Steps the Three Dukes; Great Mound holds piled corpses and death.

value.zh: 其後武庫火，西羌反。
value.en: Armory fire and Qiang revolt.
value.literal: Afterward the arsenal burned and Qiang rebelled west.

value.zh: 後五年，司空張華遇禍，賈后廢死，魯公賈謐誅。
value.en: Later Zhang Hua and Jia clan fell.
value.literal: Five years later Minister of Works Zhang Hua met disaster; Empress Jia was deposed and killed; Duke Lu Jia Mi executed.

value.zh: 又明年，趙王倫篡位。
value.en: Next year Sima Lun seized throne.
value.literal: The next year Prince Zhao Lun usurped.

value.zh: 於是三王興兵討倫，兵士戰死十餘萬人。
value.en: Princely coalition slaughtered tens of thousands.
value.literal: Then the Three Princes rose against Lun—over a hundred thousand soldiers died.

value.zh: 永康元年三月，妖星見南方。
value.en: Yongkang 1 March southern astral demon.
value.literal: In Yongkang 1 third month an evil star appeared in the south.

value.zh: 占曰：「妖星出，天下大兵將起。」
value.en: The prognostication said, "When a baleful star emerges, great war under Heaven is about to arise."
value.literal: The omen-text says: “When evil stars emerge great armies will arise.

value.zh: 是月賈后殺太子，趙王倫尋廢殺后，斬司空張華，又廢帝自立。
value.en: Jia killed heir; Lun purged court.
value.literal: That month Empress Jia killed the heir; Prince Zhao Lun soon deposed and murdered her, executed Zhang Hua, and enthroned himself.

value.zh: 於是三王並起，迭總天權。
value.en: Princes vied for power.
value.literal: Then three princes rose, trading supreme authority.

value.zh: 其十二月，彗星出牽牛之西，指天市。
value.en: December comet Herdsman to market.
value.literal: That twelfth month a comet emerged west of Herdsman pointing at Celestial Market.

value.zh: 占曰：「牛者七政始，彗出之，改元易號之象也。
value.en: The prognostication said, "Ox is the beginning of the seven regulators; when a comet emerges from it, it is the image of changing the era and altering the title.
value.literal: The omen-text says: “Ox begins the seven regulators; a comet there means changing era and reign title.

value.zh: 天市一名天府，一名天子旗，帝坐在其中。」
value.en: The Celestial Market is also called the Celestial Treasury and also the Son of Heaven’s Banner; the imperial seat is within it."
value.literal: Celestial Market is also called Celestial Treasury and Son of Heaven’s banner—the throne sits within.

value.zh: 明年，趙王倫篡位，改元，尋為大兵所滅。
value.en: Lun’s coup collapsed.
value.literal: The next year Prince Zhao Lun usurped, changed the era, then fell to great armies.

value.zh: 二年四月，彗星見齊分。
value.en: Year two April Qi comet.
value.literal: In the second year’s fourth month a comet appeared in Qi field.

value.zh: 占曰：「齊有兵喪。」
value.en: The prognostication said, "Qi will have war and mourning."
value.literal: The omen-text says: “Qi will suffer armies and mourning.

value.zh: 是時，齊王冏起兵討趙王倫。
value.en: Qi prince attacked Lun.
value.literal: Then Prince Qi Jiong rose against Prince Zhao Lun.

value.zh: 倫滅，冏擁兵不朝，專權淫奢。
value.en: Jiong tyrannized Luoyang.
value.literal: After Lun fell Jiong kept armies outside court, monopolizing power in arrogance and luxury.

value.zh: 明年，誅死。
value.en: Jiong executed next year.
value.literal: The next year he was executed.

value.zh: 惠帝元康四年九月甲午，枉矢東北行，竟天。
value.en: On jiawu in the ninth month of the fourth year of Yuankang under Emperor Hui, Crooked Arrow crossed the sky to the northeast.
value.literal: On jiawu in the ninth month of the fourth year of Yuankang under Emperor Hui, Crooked Arrow streaked northeast across the whole sky.

value.zh: 六年六月丙午夜，有枉矢自斗魁東南行。
value.en: Sixth year Crooked Arrow from Dipper.
value.literal: On bingwu midnight in the sixth year Crooked Arrow issued from Dipper handle southeastward.

value.zh: 案占曰：「以亂伐亂。
value.en: Examining the prognostication, it said, "Using disorder to attack disorder.
value.literal: Investigating the gloss: “Chaos attacks chaos.

value.zh: 北斗主執殺，出斗魁，居中執殺者，不直之象也。」
value.en: Northern Dipper governs holding and killing; when it emerges from the bowl of Dipper and the one who holds and kills occupies the center, it is the image of injustice."
value.literal: The Northern Dipper governs holding and killing; emerging from the Dipper bowl, the one who holds and kills occupying the center, is the image of injustice.

value.zh: 是後，趙王殺張、裴，廢賈后，以理太子之冤，因自篡盜，以至屠滅，以亂伐亂之應也。
value.en: Sima Lun’s purge mirrored omen.
value.literal: Afterward Prince Zhao slew Zhang and Pei, deposed Empress Jia to redress the heir—then seized power himself until extinction—chaos answering chaos.

value.zh: 一曰，氐帥齊萬年反之應也。
value.en: Alternate gloss: Qi Wannian.
value.literal: Another reading ties it to Di chieftain Qi Wannian’s rebellion.

value.zh: 《書》曰：「唐虞稽古，建官惟百。」
value.en: The Book of Documents says: "When Tang and Yu looked back to antiquity, they created no more than a hundred offices."
value.literal: The Book of Documents says: "Tang and Yu examined antiquity; they established offices numbering only one hundred."

value.zh: 所以獎導民萌，裁成庶政。
value.en: That was how they encouraged the people and gave shape to the affairs of state.
value.literal: By this means they encouraged and guided the common people, and brought order to every branch of government.

value.zh: 《易》曰：「天垂象，聖人則之。」
value.en: The Book of Changes says: "Heaven displays signs; the sage patterns himself on them."
value.literal: The Book of Changes says: "Heaven hangs forth images; the sage takes them as his model."

value.zh: 執法在南宮之右，上相處端門之外，而鳥龍居位，雲火垂名，前史詳之，其以尚矣。
value.en: Justice lay to the right of the Southern Palace; the chief minister waited beyond the Duan Gate; bird and dragon offices held rank with cloud and fire as their emblems—prior histories lay it out clearly, and the grandeur speaks for itself.
value.literal: Law sat to the right of the Southern Palace; the chief minister took station beyond the Duan Gate; the Bird and Dragon offices held their posts, cloud and fire lending their names—earlier histories spell this out in detail, and the dignity of it is plain.

value.zh: 黃帝置三公之秩，以親黎元，少昊配九扈之名，以為農正，命重黎於天地，詔融冥於水火，則可得而言焉。
value.en: The Yellow Emperor created the Three Dukes to draw near to the people; Shaohao aligned the Nine Hu titles with agricultural oversight; Chong and Li received Heaven and Earth; Zhu Rong and Ming received fire and water—and such patterns can be put into words.
value.literal: The Yellow Emperor instituted the ranks of the Three Dukes to stay close to the black-haired masses; Shaohao paired the Nine Hu bird-names with the office of director of agriculture; Chong and Li were charged with Heaven and Earth; Zhu Rong and Ming were charged with fire and water—these arrangements can indeed be described.

value.zh: 伊尹曰：「三公調陰陽，九卿通寒暑，大夫知人事，列士去其私。」
value.en: Yi Yin said: "The Three Dukes harmonize yin and yang; the Nine Ministers track the seasons; grand officers attend to human affairs; ranked officers put private interest aside."
value.literal: Yi Yin said: "The Three Dukes harmonize yin and yang; the Nine Ministers watch cold and heat; grand officers understand human affairs; ranked officers rid themselves of selfishness."

value.zh: 而成湯居亳，初置二相，以伊尹、仲虺為之，凡厥樞會，仰承君命。
value.en: When Tang of Shang made Bo his seat, he first set up two chancellors—Yi Yin and Zhong Hui—and on every pivot they carried out the sovereign's will.
value.literal: When Cheng Tang ruled from Bo, he first created two chancellors and appointed Yi Yin and Zhong Hui to them; on every critical matter they looked upward to receive the ruler's commands.

value.zh: 總及周武下車，成康垂則，六卿分職，二公弘化，咸樹司存，各題標準，苟非其道，人弗虛榮。
value.en: Under King Wu and the models left by Cheng and Kang, the Six Ministers split the labor, the Two Dukes carried royal influence abroad, every bureau had its charter, and no one claimed idle honors without the right conduct.
value.literal: Altogether, when King Wu of Zhou stepped down from his chariot to rule, Cheng and Kang handed down norms; the Six Ministers divided duties; the Two Dukes spread transformation; each office kept its place and measure; if it were not the proper Way, people did not vainly seek glory.

value.zh: 貽厥孫謀，其固本也如此。
value.en: They anchored the dynasty by planning for generations yet unborn.
value.literal: They left plans for their descendants; thus they secured the foundation.

value.zh: 及秦變周官，漢遵嬴舊，或隨時適用，或因務遷革，霸王之典，義在於斯，既獲厥安，所謂得其時制者也。
value.en: Qin refashioned Zhou's bureaucracy; Han largely kept Qin's frame while tweaking it for the moment—the logic of strong rule was there—and stability meant institutions matched their age.
value.literal: When Qin altered the Zhou offices and Han followed the Ying-clan precedent, sometimes adapting to the times, sometimes shifting with practical needs—the norms of hegemons and kings lay herein; once stability was gained, this is what is called obtaining timely institutions.

value.zh: 四征興於漢代，四安起于魏初，四鎮通於柔遠，四平止於喪亂，其渡遼、淩江，輕車、強弩，式揚遐外，用表攻伐，興而復毀，厥號彌繁。
value.en: Han invented the Four Expeditions; Wei at its outset the Four Pacifications; Four Garrisons stretched toward distant peoples; Four Peace posts vanished when chaos returned. Epithets like Crossing-the-Liao, River-Fording, light chariot, and strong crossbow brandished force beyond the borders for campaigns—created, scrapped, then multiplied until the catalogue grew tangled.
value.literal: The Four Expeditions arose in Han; the Four Pacifications began at the start of Wei; the Four Garrisons reached outward to soothe the distant; the Four Peace offices ended with turmoil and disorder; as for Crossing-the-Liao, River-Fording, light chariot, and strong crossbow—they displayed might afar and signaled campaigns—raised up and then abolished, their titles grew ever more numerous.

value.zh: 及當塗得志，克平諸夏，初有軍師祭酒，參掌戎律。
value.en: Once the Cao regime triumphed and pacified the heartland, it introduced the army adviser libationer to share oversight of military law.
value.literal: When the house at Dangtu achieved its ambition and subdued the Central Plain, there first appeared the army adviser libationer, who jointly handled military regulations.

value.zh: 建安十三年，罷漢台司，更置丞相，而以曹公居之，用兼端揆。
value.en: In the thirteenth year of Jian'an (208), the Han ministerial posts were abolished, the chancellorship was reinstated, and Lord Cao held it, thereby combining the highest civil authority.
value.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jian'an, the Han terrace ministers were abolished; the chancellor was reinstated, and Lord Cao held it, thereby combining the highest civil authority.

value.zh: 孫吳、劉蜀，多依漢制，雖復臨時命氏，而無忝舊章。
value.en: Wu and Shu largely kept Han models; occasional improvised titles notwithstanding, they stayed within the classical mold.
value.literal: Eastern Wu and Liu Bei's Shu largely followed Han institutions; though they sometimes improvised titles on the spot, they did not shame the old statutes.

value.zh: 世祖武皇帝即位之初，以安平王孚為太宰，鄭沖為太傅，王祥為太保，司馬望為太尉，何曾為司徒，荀顗為司空，石苞為大司馬，陳騫為大將軍，世所謂八公同辰，攀雲附翼者也。
value.en: At his accession, Emperor Wu named Sima Fu Grand Preceptor, Zheng Chong Grand Tutor, Wang Xiang Grand Guardian, Sima Wang Minister of War, He Zeng Minister of Education, Xun Yi Minister of Works, Shi Bao Grand Marshal, and Chen Qian Grand General—the storied eight dukes of a single hour, men who rose by riding imperial favor.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu the Shizu first ascended the throne, he appointed Prince Fu of Anping as Grand Preceptor, Zheng Chong as Grand Tutor, Wang Xiang as Grand Guardian, Sima Wang as Minister of War, He Zeng as Minister of Education, Xun Yi as Minister of Works, Shi Bao as Grand Marshal, and Chen Qian as Grand General—what the age called the eight dukes sharing one hour, climbing clouds and attaching wings.

value.zh: 若乃成乎棟宇，非一枝之勢；
value.en: Raising the whole hall takes more than one timber;
value.literal: As for completing roof-beams and rafters—it is not the strength of a single branch;

value.zh: 處乎經綸，稱萬夫之敵。
value.en: true stewardship of the realm earns the title match for ten thousand.
value.literal: to dwell in ordering the realm is to be called a match for ten thousand men.

value.zh: 或牽羊以葉於夢，或垂釣以申其道，或空桑以獻其術，或操版以啟其心。
value.en: Some arrived through dreams of sheep and grain; some through fishing metaphors; some from humble soil with a craft to sell; some by presenting the royal tablet and winning trust.
value.literal: Some led sheep and answered a leaf in a dream; some angled with a hook to proclaim their Way; some offered their arts from an empty mulberry; some grasped the tablet to open the ruler's mind.

value.zh: 臥龍飛鴻，方金擬璧，秦奚、鄭產，楚材晉用，斯亦曩時之良具，其又昭彰者焉。
value.en: Hidden dragons and soaring swans, talents weighed like gold against jade—Qin Xi, Zheng Chan, and Chu talent employed by Jin: these too were fine instruments of former times, and no less manifest.
value.literal: The sleeping dragon, the soaring wild goose—square metal compared to round jade; the shepherd of Qin, the prodigy of Zheng; Chu talent employed by Jin—these too were fine instruments of former times, and no less manifest.

value.zh: 宣王既誅曹爽，政由己出，網羅英俊，以備天官。
value.en: After Sima Yi eliminated Cao Shuang, he ruled in his own name and stocked every court post with talent.
value.literal: Once Prince Xuan had executed Cao Shuang, government proceeded from himself alone; he gathered capable men to fill the celestial offices.

value.zh: 及蘭卿受羈，貴公顯戮，雖復策名魏氏，而乃心皇晉。
value.en: When fine officers were seized and great nobles died in public execution, names might still stand with Wei but hearts had already turned to Jin.
value.literal: When worthy ministers were placed under restraint and eminent dukes suffered public execution—though they still bore registration under the Wei, their hearts were with the august Jin.

value.zh: 及文王纂業，初啟晉台，始置二衛，有前驅養由之弩；
value.en: When Sima Zhao extended the family work and founded the Jin apparatus, he created the Two Guards with vanguard crossbows worthy of Yang Youji.
value.literal: When King Wen continued the enterprise and first opened the Jin terrace, he began setting up the Two Guards, including front-vanguard crossbows like Yang Youji's.

value.zh: 及設三部，有熊渠佽飛之眾。
value.en: When the Three Corps were established, there were masses like those of Xiong Qu and Ci Fei.
value.literal: When the Three Departments were established, there were masses like the royal swimmers of Xiong Qu.

value.zh: 是以武帝龍飛，乘茲奮翼，猶武王以周之十亂而理殷民者也。
value.en: Thus Emperor Wu's rise—vaulting on these preparations—matched King Wu deploying his ten able assistants to rule the former Shang subjects.
value.literal: Therefore when Emperor Wu ascended like a dragon, riding this to beat his wings, it was like King Wu of Zhou using the Zhou's ten ministers to govern the Yin people.

value.zh: 是以泰始盡于太康，喬柯茂葉，來居斯位；
value.en: From the Taishi era through Taikang, imposing figures filled those ranks;
value.literal: Thus from Taishi through Taikang, tall trees with lush foliage came to occupy these posts;

value.zh: 自太興訖於建元，南金北銑，用處茲秩。
value.en: from Daxing to Jianyuan, the finest metal south and north filled those offices.
value.literal: from Daxing down to Jianyuan, southern gold and northern ore were employed in these ranks.

value.zh: 雖未擬乎夔拊龍言，天工人代，亦庶幾乎任官惟賢，蒞事惟能者也。
value.en: They fell short of the sage-kings' marriage of Heaven's work to human agency, yet they neared the ideal: office by virtue, tasks by competence.
value.literal: Though they did not equal Kui's drumming and Long's pronouncements—Heaven's work and man's substitute—they approximated appoint officials only for worth, approach affairs only by ability.

value.zh: 丞相、相國，並秦官也。
value.en: The titles chancellor and minister of state both originated in Qin.
value.literal: Chancellor and minister of state were both Qin offices.

value.zh: 晉受魏禪，並不置，自惠帝之後，省置無恆。
value.en: Jin left both vacant at the founding; after Emperor Hui the posts flickered in and out without a fixed rule.
value.literal: When Jin received Wei's abdication, neither was established; from Emperor Hui onward, abolition and establishment were not constant.

value.zh: 為之者，趙王倫、梁王肜、成都王穎、南陽王保、王敦、王導之徒，皆非復尋常人臣之職。
value.en: When princes such as Sima Lun, Sima Rong, Sima Ying, Sima Bao, Wang Dun, and Wang Dao took these titles, they wielded power far beyond an ordinary subject's charge.
value.literal: Those who held them—Zhao Wang Lun, Liang Wang Rong, Chengdu Wang Ying, Nanyang Wang Bao, Wang Dun, Wang Dao, and the like—were no longer the duties of ordinary ministers.

value.zh: 言之不從，是謂不乂
value.en: When commands find no compliance, the canon calls it a failure of proper order.
value.literal: When commands find no compliance, the canon calls it a failure of proper order.

value.zh: 趙王倫廢惠帝于金墉城，改號金墉城為永安宮。
value.en: Sima Lun cast Emperor Hui into Jinyong and cynically rebranded the prison Yong'an.
value.literal: Prince Zhao Sima Lun deposed Emperor Hui at Jinyong fortress and renamed the fortress Yong'an Palace.

value.zh: 帝尋復位而倫誅。
value.en: Hui returned; Lun went to the block.
value.literal: The emperor soon regained the throne and Lun was executed.

value.zh: 桓玄初改年為大亨，遐邇歡言曰「二月了」，故義謀以仲春發也。
value.en: Huan Xuan first changed the era to Daheng; far and near gleefully said "the second month is over," therefore the loyal plot rose in mid-spring.
value.literal: Huan Xuan first changed the era to Daheng; far and near gleefully said "the second month is over," therefore the loyal plot rose in mid-spring.

value.zh: 玄篡立，又改年為建始，以與趙王倫同，又易為永始，永始復是王莽受封之年也。
value.en: His usurpation recycled Sima Lun's Jianshi, then Wang Mang's Yongshi — compounding ill-omened names.
value.literal: When Xuan usurped, he changed the era to Jianshi — the same as Prince Zhao Lun — then switched to Yongshi; Yongshi was likewise the year Wang Mang received his fief.

value.zh: 始徙司馬道子于安成。
value.en: Sima Daozi was packed off to Ancheng to clear the stage.
value.literal: First Sima Daozi was banished to Ancheng.

value.zh: 安帝遜位，出永安宮，封為平固王，琅邪王德文為石陽公，並使住尋陽城。
value.en: An-di abdicated from Yong'an, won a hollow title at Pinggu, while Langya Wang Dewen became duke of Shiyang — both exiled to Xunyang.
value.literal: Emperor An abdicated, left Yong'an Palace, was enfeoffed Prince of Pinggu; Langya Wang Dewen became Duke of Shiyang; both were ordered to reside in Xunyang city.

value.zh: 識者皆以為言不從之妖僭也。
value.en: Every augur read the clumsy reign titles as arrogance and deceitful speech.
value.literal: Those who understood omens all deemed it demonic presumption — words again not obeyed.

value.zh: 永甯元年，自夏及秋，青、徐、幽、并四州旱。
value.en: Yongning 1 scorched four provinces from midsummer into fall.
value.literal: First Yongning year: from summer through autumn drought in Qing, Xu, You, and Bing provinces.

value.zh: 十二月，又郡國十二旱。
value.en: Winter brought a dozen more drought reports.
value.literal: Twelfth month — again twelve commanderies and states drought.

value.zh: 是年春，三王討趙王倫，六旬之中數十戰，死者十餘萬人。
value.en: The war on Sima Lun killed over a hundred thousand in two months.
value.literal: That spring the three kings campaigned against Prince Zhao Lun; within sixty days dozens of battles, more than a hundred thousand dead.

value.zh: 元康中，京洛童謠曰：「南風起，吹白沙，遙望魯國何嵯峨，千歲髑髏生齒牙。」
value.en: In Yuankang the capital children sang: "South wind rises, blows white sand; far off how steep the state of Lu — thousand-year skulls sprout teeth."
value.literal: In Yuankang the capital children sang: "South wind rises, blows white sand; far off how steep the state of Lu — thousand-year skulls sprout teeth."

value.zh: 又曰：「城東馬子莫嚨哅，此至來年纏女閤。」
value.en: It also said: "East-city colt, don't whinny — by next year you'll tangle in women's boudoirs."
value.literal: It also said: "East-city colt, don't whinny — by next year you'll tangle in women's boudoirs."

value.zh: 南風，賈后字也。
value.en: Nanfeng was the empress's sobriquet.
value.literal: South wind" is Empress Jia's style name.

value.zh: 白，晉行也。
value.en: White stood for metal — Jin's element.
value.literal: "White" is Jin's phase color.

value.zh: 沙門，太子小名也。
value.en: "Monkling" was Sima Zhong's pet name.
value.literal: "Shamen" is the heir apparent's childhood name.

value.zh: 魯，賈謐國也。
value.en: Lu mapped onto Jia Mi's noble seat.
value.literal: "Lu" is Jia Mi's princedom.

value.zh: 言賈后將與謐為亂，以危太子，而趙王因釁咀嚼豪賢，以成篡奪，不得其死之應也。
value.en: The gloss tied the verses to Jia's coup plot and Sima Lun's coming slaughter.
value.literal: It means Empress Jia would riot with Mi to endanger the heir, while Prince Zhao would chew up great men and seize the throne — an omen of dying badly.

value.zh: 元康中，天下商農通著大鄣日。
value.en: Yuankang fashion made everyone don huge visors.
value.literal: In Yuankang merchants and farmers all wore wide sun-hats.

value.zh: 時童謠曰：「屠蘇鄣日覆兩耳，當見瞎兒作天子。」
value.en: A rhyme said: "Tusu hat brim covers both ears — soon a blind boy will be Son of Heaven."
value.literal: A rhyme said: "Tusu hat brim covers both ears — soon a blind boy will be Son of Heaven."

value.zh: 及趙王倫篡位，其目實眇焉。
value.en: Sima Lun's bad eye matched the "blind boy" line.
value.literal: When Prince Zhao Lun usurped, his eye was indeed blind.

value.zh: 趙王倫既篡，洛中童謠曰：「獸從北來鼻頭汗，龍從南來登城看，水從西來河灌灌。」
value.en: After Prince Zhao seized power, Luoyang sang: "Beasts come from the north with sweaty snouts; dragons from the south climb walls to look; water from the west makes rivers boil."
value.literal: After Prince Zhao seized power, Luoyang sang: "Beasts come from the north with sweaty snouts; dragons from the south climb walls to look; water from the west makes rivers boil."

value.zh: 數月而齊王、成都、河間義兵同會誅倫。
value.en: The allied princes purged Sima Lun within the year.
value.literal: Within months Qi, Chengdu, and Hejian righteous hosts jointly executed Lun.

value.zh: 案成都西籓而在鄴，故曰「獸從北來。」
value.en: Chengdu was a western fief but sat at Ye — hence "beasts from the north."
value.literal: Chengdu was a western fief but sat at Ye — hence "beasts from the north."

value.zh: 齊東籓而在許，故曰「龍從南來。」
value.en: Qi was an eastern fief but camped at Xu — hence "dragons from the south."
value.literal: Qi was an eastern fief but camped at Xu — hence "dragons from the south."

value.zh: 河間水源而在關中，故曰「水從西來」。
value.en: Hejian drew water from Guanzhong — hence "water from the west."
value.literal: Hejian drew water from Guanzhong — hence "water from the west."

value.zh: 齊留輔政，居於宮西，又有無君之心，故言「登城看」也。
value.en: Qi stayed to assist government, dwelling west of the palace, yet nursed disloyalty — hence "climb walls to look."
value.literal: Qi stayed to assist government, dwelling west of the palace, yet nursed disloyalty — hence "climb walls to look."

value.zh: 惠帝永康元年，趙王倫既篡，京師得異鳥，莫能名。
value.en: In Yongkang 1 under Emperor Hui, after Sima Lun’s usurpation, the capital captured an unnamed strange bird.
value.literal: Emperor Hui, Yongkang 1 — after Prince Lun of Zhao had usurped, a strange bird was obtained in the capital, and no one could name it.

value.zh: 倫使人持出，周旋城邑市以問人。
value.en: Paraded the bird for identification.
value.literal: Lun had it carried through city markets asking everyone.

value.zh: 積日，宮西有小兒見之，遂自言曰：「服留鳥翳。」
value.en: After days a western-slum boy saw it and said: "It is the 'stay-cloak' bird."
value.literal: After days a western-slum boy saw it and said: "It is the 'stay-cloak' bird."

value.zh: 持者即還白倫，倫使更求，又見之，乃將入宮，密籠鳥，並閉小兒戶中，明日視之，悉不見。
value.en: Lun imprisoned bird and prophet — both disappeared.
value.literal: The bearer reported to Lun; Lun sent to find him again, caged the bird with the boy locked in; next day both vanished.

value.zh: 此羽蟲之孽。
value.en: Another winged portent.
value.literal: This was feathered calamity.

value.zh: 時趙王倫有目瘤之疾，言服留者，謂倫留將服其罪也。
value.en: The pun foretold Lun's execution.
value.literal: Then Prince Zhao Lun had an eye tumor; "stay-cloak" meant Lun would soon suffer punishment.

value.zh: 尋而倫誅。
value.en: Sima Lun fell quickly.
value.literal: Soon Lun was executed.

value.zh: 趙王倫篡位，有鶉入太極殿，雉集東堂。
value.en: Game birds invaded the throne hall.
value.literal: When Prince Zhao Lun usurped, quail entered Taiji Hall, pheasants gathered east hall.

value.zh: 天戒若曰，太極東堂皆朝享聽政之所，而鶉雉同日集之者，趙王倫不當居此位也。
value.en: Twin fowl barred his legitimacy.
value.literal: Heaven warns: Taiji and east hall are where court meets — quail and pheasant the same day means Lun must not occupy that seat.

value.zh: 《詩》云：「鵲之強強，鶉之奔奔，人之無良，我以為君。」
value.en: The Book of Songs says: "Magpie strong-strong, quail darting — the man lacks goodness — I make him lord."
value.literal: The Book of Songs says: "Magpie strong-strong, quail darting — the man lacks goodness — I make him lord."

value.zh: 其此之謂乎！
value.en: Editors applied the ode to Lun.
value.literal: Did it not mean this?

value.zh: 尋而倫誅。
value.en: He died as foretold.
value.literal: Soon Lun was executed.

value.zh: 陳騫
value.en: Chen Qian
value.literal: Chen Qian

value.zh: 初，趙王倫諂事賈后，頠甚惡之，倫數求官，頠與張華復固執不許，由是深為倫所怨。
value.en: Sima Lun curried Jia Nanfeng's favor while Yi and Zhang Hua blocked his offices, planting a deadly grudge.
value.literal: At first the Prince of Zhao, Sima Lun, fawned on Empress Jia; Yi loathed him. Lun repeatedly sought promotion; Yi and Zhang Hua steadfastly refused—thereby earning Lun's bitter hatred.

value.zh: 倫又潛懷篡逆，欲先除朝望，因廢賈后之際遂誅之，時年三十四。
value.en: Lun used Jia's fall as cover to murder Yi at thirty-four while plotting a coup.
value.literal: Lun also nursed usurpation: wishing first to eliminate eminent ministers, he executed Yi while deposing the empress; Yi was thirty-four.

value.zh: 二子嵩、該，倫亦欲害之。
value.en: Lun targeted Yi's sons Song and Gai next.
value.literal: His sons Song and Gai—Lun meant to kill them too.

value.zh: 梁王肜、東海王越稱頠父秀有勳王室，配食太廟，不宜滅其後嗣，故得不死，徙帶方；
value.en: Princes Sima Rong of Liang and Sima Yue of Donghai declared that Yi's father Xiu had served the dynasty and received offerings in the Grand Temple—his line must not be extinguished—so the boys lived on, banished to Daifang.
value.literal: Princes Sima Rong of Liang and Sima Yue of Donghai declared that Yi's father Xiu had served the dynasty and received offerings in the Grand Temple—his line must not be extinguished—so the boys lived on, banished to Daifang.

value.zh: 惠帝反正，追復頠本官，改葬以卿禮，諡曰成。
value.en: After Hui's restoration Yi won reinstatement, a proper reburial, and the posthumous name Cheng.
value.literal: When Emperor Hui was restored, Yi's offices were posthumously reinstated; he was reburied with ministerial ceremony and titled Cheng.

value.zh: 以嵩嗣爵，為中書黃門侍郎。
value.en: The marquisate passed to Song in the central secretariat.
value.literal: Song inherited the title and became palace attendant and palace secretary.

value.zh: 該出後從伯凱，為散騎常侍，並為乞活賊陳午所害。
value.en: Gai had been adopted out to his father's cousin Kai; he was supernumerary attendant until both brothers fell to Chen Wu's Qi Huo band.
value.literal: Gai had been adopted out to his father's cousin Kai; he was supernumerary attendant until both brothers fell to Chen Wu's Qi Huo band.

value.zh: 安平獻王孚
value.en: Prince Xian of Anping, Sima Fu.
value.literal: Prince Fu of Anping with posthumous title Xian (section heading).

value.zh: 威字景曜，初嗣洪，
value.en: Sima Wei, styled Jingyao, first inherited Hong.
value.literal: Wei courtesy Jingyao at first succeeded Hong.

value.zh: 咸寧三年，徙封章武。
value.en: In Xianning year three, his fief was transferred to Zhangwu.
value.literal: In Xianning year three, his fief was transferred to Zhangwu.

value.zh: 太康九年，嗣義陽王望。
value.en: In Taikang year nine, he continued Sima Wang's Yiyang princedom.
value.literal: In Taikang year nine, he continued Sima Wang's Yiyang princedom.

value.zh: 威凶暴無操行，諂附趙王倫。
value.en: Savage and unscrupulous, he hitched himself to Sima Lun.
value.literal: Wei was fierce and violent without moral conduct and flattered and attached himself to Prince Zhao Lun.

value.zh: 元康末，為散騎常侍，倫將篡，使威與黃門郎駱休逼帝奪璽綬，倫以威為中書令。
value.en: Late in Yuankang he helped Sima Lun wrench the seal from Emperor Hui alongside Luo Xiu, then took the palace secretariat.
value.literal: At the end of Yuankang he was irregular cavalry attendant; when Lun was about to usurp he sent Wei together with Yellow Gate Gentleman Luo Xiu to coerce the emperor and seize the seal cords; Lun appointed Wei Palace Secretariat Director.

value.zh: 倫敗，惠帝反正，曰：「阿皮捩吾指，奪吾璽綬，不可不殺。」
value.en: When Lun was defeated Emperor Hui resumed right rule and said, 'Api twisted my fingers and seized my seal cords—cannot fail to kill him.'
value.literal: When Lun was defeated Emperor Hui resumed right rule and said, 'Api twisted my fingers and seized my seal cords—cannot fail to kill him.'

value.zh: 阿皮，威小字也。
value.en: Api' was Wei's infant name.
value.literal: Api was Wei's childhood name.

value.zh: 於是誅威。
value.en: Wei was put to death.
value.literal: Thereupon Wei was executed.

value.zh: 楙善諂諛，曲事楊駿。
value.en: Sima Mao excelled at sycophancy and curried favor with Yang Jun.
value.literal: Mao was skilled at flattery and fawning and bent his service to Yang Jun.

value.zh: 及駿誅，依法當死，東安公繇與楙善，故得不坐。
value.en: Jun's fall should have cost Mao his life, yet Sima You's friendship shielded him.
value.literal: When Jun was executed, by law Mao ought to have died, but Duke of Dongan You was friendly with Mao, so he avoided punishment.

value.zh: 尋遷大鴻臚，加侍中。
value.en: He soon rose to grand herald with supernumerary palace attendant rank.
value.literal: Soon he was promoted Grand Herald and added palace attendant.

value.zh: 繇欲擅朝政，與汝南王亮不平。
value.en: Sima You grasped for centralized power and clashed with Prince Liang of Runan.
value.literal: You wished to monopolize court government and was at odds with Prince Liang of Runan.

value.zh: 帝托以繇討駿顧望，免繇、楙等官，遣楙就國。
value.en: Emperor Hui blamed Sima You for half-hearted action against Jun, cashiered both men, and banished Mao to his domain.
value.literal: The emperor on the pretext that You hesitated in attacking Jun removed You and Mao from office and sent Mao to his fief.

value.zh: 楙殖財貨，奢僭逾制。
value.en: He hoarded treasure and flouted sumptuary law with pretensions beyond his rank.
value.literal: Mao amassed wealth and goods; extravagance and usurpation of ritual exceeded regulations.

value.zh: 趙王倫篡位，召還。
value.en: Sima Lun's coup brought Mao back to court.
value.literal: When Prince Zhao Lun usurped the throne he recalled Mao.

value.zh: 及義兵起，倫以楙為衛將軍、都督諸軍事。
value.en: Once loyalist armies rose Lun named Mao metropolitan guard and overall commander.
value.literal: When the righteous host rose, Lun appointed Mao General Who Guards the Metropolis and supervisor of all military affairs.

value.zh: 倫敗，楙免官。
value.en: Lun's fall stripped Mao of his posts.
value.literal: When Lun was defeated Mao was dismissed from office.

value.zh: 齊王冏輔政，繇復為僕射，舉楙為平東將軍、都督徐州諸軍事，鎮下邳。
value.en: Under Sima Jiong's regency Sima You returned as vice director and nominated Mao as pacifier-general for Xu based at Xiapi.
value.literal: When Prince of Qi Jiong assisted government You again became vice director and recommended Mao as General Who Pacifies the East and supervisor of Xu military affairs, stationed at Xiapi.

value.zh: 成都王穎輔政，進楙為衛將軍。
value.en: Sima Ying's turn at power promoted Mao to metropolitan guard.
value.literal: When Prince of Chengdu Ying assisted government Mao was advanced to General Who Guards the Metropolis.

value.zh: 彭城穆王權，字子輿，宣帝弟魏魯相東武城侯馗之子也。
value.en: Sima Quan, King Mu of Pengcheng and styled Ziyu, was the son of Sima Kui, Marquis of Dongwucheng and governor of Lu under Wei, who was Sima Yi's younger brother.
value.literal: Prince Mu of Pengcheng Quan courtesy Ziyu was son of Emperor Xuan's younger brother Wei Lu governor East Wucheng Marquis Kui.

value.zh: 初襲封，拜冗從僕射。
value.en: He opened as supernumerary chariot master.
value.literal: At first inheriting the enfeoffment he was appointed Supernumerary Master of Chariots.

value.zh: 武帝受禪，封彭城王，邑二千九百戶。
value.en: Sima Yan made him Pengcheng prince at 2,900 households.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Pengcheng with two thousand nine hundred households.

value.zh: 出為北中郎將、都督鄴城守諸軍事。
value.en: He commanded Ye's northern gentleman garrison.
value.literal: He went out as General of the Northern Gentlemen supervising Ye city garrison affairs.

value.zh: 泰始中入朝，賜袞冕之服。
value.en: Mid-Taishi brought court investiture robes.
value.literal: In Taishi mid-years he entered court and was granted robe and crown of state.

value.zh: 咸甯元年薨，子元王植立。
value.en: 275 death; Yuan prince Zhi followed.
value.literal: In Xianning year one he died; son Prince Yuan Zhi succeeded.

value.zh: 歷位後將軍，尋拜國子祭酒、太僕卿、侍中、尚書。
value.en: His offices ran rear general, academy libationer, coach minister, palace attendant, and ministry.
value.literal: He successively held Later General, soon appointed Libationer of the Imperial Academy, Minister of Coachmanship, palace attendant, and minister of writing.

value.zh: 出為安東將軍、都督揚州諸軍事，代淮南王允鎮壽春，未發。
value.en: Named east-pacifier for Yangzhou replacing Yun at Shouchun, he never took up post.
value.literal: He was going out as General Who Pacifies the East supervising Yangzhou military affairs replacing Prince Huainan Yun at Shouchun but did not depart.

value.zh: 或云植助允攻趙王倫，遂以憂薨。
value.en: Tradition claims he aided Yun against Sima Lun and died of anxiety.
value.literal: Some say Zhi assisted Yun in attacking Prince Zhao Lun and therefore died of grief.

value.zh: 贈車騎將軍，增封萬五千戶。
value.en: The court added posthumous chariot-and-cavalry honors and boosted his fief by fifteen thousand households.
value.literal: He was posthumously invested chariot-and-cavalry general and his enfeoffment was increased by fifteen thousand households.

value.zh: 子康王釋立，官至南中郎將、持節、平南將軍，分魯國蕃、薛二縣以益其國，心二萬三千戶。
value.en: Prince Kang Sima Shi rose to southern gentleman-general with pacifying-south command, annexed Fan and Xue from Lu, and held twenty-three thousand households.
value.literal: Son Prince Kang Shi succeeded; he reached Southern Gentlemen General, credential-bearing, Pacifying South General; partitioned Fan and Xue counties of Lu to enlarge his state; total twenty-three thousand households.

value.zh: 薨，子雄立，坐奔蘇峻伏誅，更以釋子紘嗣。
value.en: After his death Xiong inherited but died with Su Jun's rebellion; Hong, son of Shi, continued the line.
value.literal: He died; son Xiong succeeded; Xiong was executed for fleeing to Su Jun; Shi's son Hong was changed to succeed.

value.zh: 魏舒，字陽元，任城樊人也。
value.en: Wei Shu, whose courtesy name was Yangyuan, came from Fan in Rencheng commandery.
value.literal: Wei Shu, courtesy name Yangyuan, was a man of Fan in Rencheng.

value.zh: 少孤，為外家寧氏所養。
value.en: He lost his father while still young and was brought up by his mother's people, the Nings.
value.literal: In youth he was orphaned and was reared by his maternal kin, the Ning clan.

value.zh: 寧氏起宅，相宅者云：「當出貴甥。」
value.en: When the Nings raised a new house, a geomancer told them, "This site will produce a distinguished nephew."
value.literal: The Ning family built a house, and a geomancer of the site said, "A noble nephew will come forth."

value.zh: 外祖母以魏氏甥小而慧，意謂應之。
value.en: His maternal grandmother, seeing that the Wei boy was young but bright, assumed the omen pointed to him.
value.literal: His maternal grandmother, because the Wei nephew was small yet clever, in her mind thought it referred to him.

value.zh: 舒曰：「當為外氏成此宅相。」
value.en: Shu said, "It falls to me to fulfill that houselot prophecy for our mother's family."
value.literal: Shu said, "I shall for the maternal clan complete this houselot omen."

value.zh: 久乃別居。
value.en: Only after many years did he move out and keep a separate household.
value.literal: After a long time then he lived apart.

value.zh: 身長八尺二寸，姿望秀偉，飲酒石餘，而遲鈍質樸，不為鄉親所重。
value.en: He stood eight chi and two cun tall, carried himself with striking presence, and could put away more than a shi of wine, yet he seemed slow and unpolished, so neighbors and relatives thought little of him.
value.literal: His body was eight chi two cun in height, his bearing fine and grand, he drank more than a shi of wine, yet was slow, dull, plain, and was not esteemed by townsmen and kin.

value.zh: 從叔父吏部郎衡，有名當世，亦不之知，使守水碓，每歎曰：「舒堪數百戶長，我願畢矣！」
value.en: His paternal uncle Heng, a Personnel Ministry officer celebrated in their day, never recognized his gifts either and set him to mind the water-powered mill, sighing, "If Shu can serve as headman over a few hundred households, I shall ask nothing more!"
value.literal: His father's cousin Heng, Personnel Ministry gentleman, had fame in the age, also did not know him, made him guard the water trip-hammer, and often sighed, saying, "Shu can suffice as chief of several hundred households — my wishes are fulfilled!"

value.zh: 舒亦不以介意。
value.en: Shu did not resent him for it.
value.literal: Shu also did not on that account take it to mind.

value.zh: 不修常人之節，不為皎曆之事，每欲容才長物，終不顯人之短。
value.en: He scorned petty convention and avoided ostentatious moralism, preferring always to nurture others' strengths and never to expose their faults.
value.literal: He did not cultivate ordinary men's scruples, did not do bright-harsh matters, always wished to accommodate talent and lengthen things, and to the end did not display people's shortcomings.

value.zh: 性好騎射，著韋衣。
value.en: He loved riding and archery and habitually dressed in leather hunting clothes.
value.literal: By nature he loved riding and shooting, and wore leather garments.

value.zh: 入山澤，以漁獵為事。
value.en: He roamed hills and wetlands and made fishing and hunting his chief pastime.
value.literal: He entered mountains and marshes and took fishing and hunting as his occupation.

value.zh: 唯太原王乂謂舒曰：「卿終當為台輔，然今未能令妻子免饑寒，吾當助卿營之。」
value.en: Wang Yi of Taiyuan alone told him, "You are destined for the highest councils of state, yet you cannot yet keep your wife and children from want; let me help you set them up."
value.literal: Only Wang Yi of Taiyuan said to Shu, "You in the end will become a pillar minister, yet now are not able to cause wife and children to escape cold and hunger; I shall help you arrange it."

value.zh: 常振其匱乏，舒受而不辭。
value.en: Wang regularly supplied what the household lacked, and Shu accepted without demur.
value.literal: He regularly relieved their want; Shu accepted and did not decline.

value.zh: 舒嘗詣野王，主人妻夜產，俄而聞車馬之聲，相問曰：「男也，女也？」
value.en: On a visit to Yewang, while his host's wife labored in the night, voices like chariots and horses suddenly sounded outside, asking, "Boy or girl?"
value.literal: Shu once went to Yewang; the host's wife gave birth in the night; presently they heard the sound of horses and chariots, mutually asking, "Male or female?"

value.zh: 曰：「男，書之，十五以兵死。」
value.en: The answer came: "A son. Record it—he will die by the sword at fifteen."
value.literal: It was said, "Male; write it; at fifteen he will die by weapons."

value.zh: 復問：「寢者為誰？」
value.en: Then they asked, "Who lies abed here?"
value.literal: Again they asked, "Who is the one sleeping?"

value.zh: 曰：「魏公舒。」
value.en: The reply was, "Lord Wei Shu."
value.literal: It was said, "Lord Wei Shu."

value.zh: 後十五載，詣主人，問所生兒何在，曰：「因條桑為斧傷而死。」
value.en: Fifteen years later he looked up the host and asked after that child; the man said, "He died when an axe slipped as he was pruning mulberry."
value.literal: After fifteen years he went to the host, asked where the born child was, and it was said, "Because trimming mulberry he was wounded by an axe and died."

value.zh: 舒自知當為公矣。
value.en: Shu understood then that he was fated to rise to the rank of duke.
value.literal: Shu himself knew he would become a duke.

value.zh: 高光，字宣茂，陳留圉城人，魏太尉柔之子也。
value.en: Gao Guang, courtesy name Xuanmao, was a native of Yucheng in Chenliu, the son of Grand Commandant Gao Rou of Wei.
value.literal: Gao Guang, courtesy name Xuanmao, was a man of Yucheng in Chenliu, son of Wei Grand Commandant Rou.

value.zh: 光少習家業，明練刑理。
value.en: From youth he trained in his family's legal tradition and became expert in penal law.
value.literal: Guang in youth practiced the family occupation, was clear and practiced in punishments and principles.

value.zh: 初以太子舍人累遷尚書郎，出為幽州刺史、潁州太守。
value.en: He began as household gentleman to the heir apparent and rose to gentleman of the masters of writing, then became inspector of You province and governor of Yingzhou commandery.
value.literal: At first as householder to the heir apparent by accumulated transfers became Secretariat gentleman, went out as Inspector of You Province, governor of Yingzhou.

value.zh: 是時武帝置黃沙獄，以典詔囚。
value.en: At that time Emperor Wu founded the Yellow Sand prison for prisoners sentenced by imperial edict.
value.literal: At this time Emperor Wu established Yellow Sand prison, to manage edict prisoners.

value.zh: 以光曆世明法，用為黃沙御史，秩與中丞同，遷廷尉。
value.en: Because his family had long mastered the code, Guang was named censor of Yellow Sand with rank equal to the palace assistant secretary, then promoted director of justice.
value.literal: Because Guang through generations understood law, he was used as Yellow Sand censor; rank was the same as the palace assistant secretary; he was promoted Director of Justice.

value.zh: 元康中，拜尚書，典三公曹。
value.en: During Yuankang he was appointed minister of the masters of writing in charge of the Three Dukes section.
value.literal: In Yuankang he was appointed Minister of the Secretariat, in charge of the Three Dukes bureau.

value.zh: 時趙王倫篡逆，光於其際，守道全貞。
value.en: When Sima Lun, prince of Zhao, usurped the throne, Guang held to principle and kept his integrity intact.
value.literal: When Prince of Zhao Lun usurped and rebelled, Guang at that juncture kept the Way and preserved integrity.

value.zh: 及倫賜死，齊王冏輔政，復以光為廷尉，遷尚書，加奉車都尉。
value.en: After Lun was forced to take his life and Prince Jiong of Qi directed the government, Guang was again named director of justice, then minister of the masters of writing with the added title colonel who conducts the carriage.
value.literal: When Lun was ordered to die, Prince of Qi Jiong assisted governance; again they made Guang Director of Justice, promoted Minister of the Secretariat, added Colonel Who Conducts the Carriage.

value.zh: 後從駕討成都王穎有勳，封延陵縣公，邑千八百戶。
value.en: Later he accompanied the imperial train against Prince Ying of Chengdu and earned distinction; he was enfeoffed as duke of Yanling county with one thousand eight hundred households.
value.literal: Later following the carriage in punishing Prince of Chengdu Ying he had merit; he was enfeoffed duke of Yanling county, fief one thousand eight hundred households.

value.zh: 于時朝廷咸推光明于用法，故頻典理官。
value.en: The whole court acknowledged his clarity in applying the law, so he was repeatedly placed over the judiciary.
value.literal: At that time the court all pushed Guang as clear in applying law; therefore repeatedly he managed judicial offices.

value.zh: 惠帝為張方所逼，幸長安，朝臣奔散，莫有從者，光獨侍帝而西。
value.en: When Emperor Hui was driven by Zhang Fang to take refuge in Chang'an and the court fled in panic with none willing to follow, Guang alone accompanied the emperor westward.
value.literal: Emperor Hui was pressed by Zhang Fang, traveled to Chang'an; court ministers ran and scattered; none had followers; Guang alone attended the emperor going west.

value.zh: 遷尚書左僕射，加散騎常侍。
value.en: He was promoted left vice-director of the masters of writing with the added title cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.
value.literal: He was promoted Left Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, added Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

value.zh: 光兄誕為上官巳等所用，曆徐、雍二州刺史。
value.en: Guang's elder brother Dan was employed by Shangguan Si and his faction and served as inspector of Xu and Yong provinces in turn.
value.literal: Guang's elder brother Dan was used by Shangguan Si and others, successively was Inspector of Xu and Yong provinces.

value.zh: 誕性任放無倫次，而決烈過人，與光異操。
value.en: Dan was wild and unmethodical, yet bolder than most—a temper quite unlike his brother's.
value.literal: Dan's nature was unbridled and unrestrained without order, yet decisive and fierce surpassing others; with Guang his conduct differed.

value.zh: 常謂光小節，恆輕侮之，光事誕愈謹。
value.en: He constantly mocked Guang for fussiness and treated him with contempt, yet Guang served his elder brother with growing deference.
value.literal: He always called Guang petty scruples, constantly treated him lightly and insulted him; Guang serving Dan became more careful.
